metadata.note: The original Norfolk Southern (1883-1974; NOT the 1982 Norfolk Southern, which is a different company with its own string 'Norfolk Southern Railway' elsewhere in data/), and its namesake predecessor the Elizabeth City and Norfolk (1881-1883). Drawn from research/branches/norfolk_southern_railway_original.txt in the site repo (DanielMConnolly/historical-trains) (2026-10-08). Before this layer the map drew no part of this railroad. Only the report's drawable spans are drawn, which keep to years a source confirms. Company string 'Norfolk Southern Railway (1883–1974)' with label 'Norfolk Southern (1883–1974)' so Rule 4 cannot merge it with the 1982 company. Its 1883/1891/1906/1910/1942 renames are receivership reorganizations of one operator and share one colour. The Elizabeth City & Norfolk -> Norfolk Southern change of 1 Feb 1883 was a rename of the same company; it is drawn as its own feature (own colour) because trains ran under the EC&N name 1881-1883. The Atlantic & North Carolina lease-era feature (1908-1932) takes the NS colour because the NS ran the trains. The Virginia Beach and Cape Henry divisions are split by MODE at 1904 and 1935 (steam / electric interurban / gas-electric rail cars). Last NS passenger train 31 Jan 1948; everything after is freight only (Feb 1952 Official Guide) and not drawn. Seven branches end at the NCUC's May 1938 discontinuance order, not at their abandonment years.

geometry_caveats: Straight-line legs (all named in each feature's geometry_quality): Bridgeton - Bayboro 14.6 mi and Bayboro - Oriental 9.6 mi (no geometry anywhere); Star - Asheboro two chords 4.1 + 3.9 mi; Valhalla - Edenton 3.7 mi; Ellerbe approach 2.2 mi; Bayside shore on the Cape Henry line ~4.1 mi; Cavalier link 0.9 mi.

Norfolk approaches are not drawn: the main line starts at Berkley (the 1881 and post-1940 terminal), the Cape Henry line at Ballentine Place; the main line's c.1891-1940 trackage-rights run into Park Avenue / Norfolk Terminal Station is omitted.
Aberdeen - Asheboro is 15% short of Fowler's 65.0 mi; his mileposts suggest an earlier routing via Jackson Springs. Pinehurst draws the c.1925 relocation for all years.
Albemarle Sound trestle from OHM may be the 1960-63 rebuild.
not_yet_sourced: End years that are the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end ([OPEN]): Raleigh - Charlotte 1938; Mackeys - Bishop Cross 1919; Jackson Springs 1922; A&NC lease and Beaufort extension 1932; Cape Henry north shore 1933; Cape Henry beach section 1946.

Start years that are the first CONFIRMED year, not the opening ([OPEN]): Mackeys - Washington 1906; Washington - Zebulon 1908; Marsden - New Bern 1909; Bayboro - Oriental 1911; Mackeys - Bishop Cross and Bishop Cross - Belhaven 1906; Columbia 1911; Suffolk - Edenton 1919; Fayetteville 1914; Aberdeen - Asheboro and Jackson Springs 1913; A&NC lease and Beaufort 1908.
Single proven years ([ANCHOR]): Pinetown cutoff 1938; Candor - Ellerbe 1923; Pinehurst - Carthage 1913.
Raleigh - Charlotte end: the NCUC decision on the 1938 discontinuance petition was not found (gone by 1942).
The May 1938 order was an authorization; no 'last mixed train' report was found for any of the seven branches.
Virginia portions: no Virginia SCC order for the Suffolk end of the Suffolk District; Cape Henry north-shore and Munden end dates unknown.
Virginia Beach Division end: 1947 (Wikipedia NS, Fowler, virginiaplaces) vs 1948 (Wikipedia, Transportation in Virginia Beach). 1947 drawn.
A&NC lease dates: lease 1 Sep 1904 vs NS 'took over' 1906 vs 'leased 1907'; end 1934 'forfeited' vs 1935 default. No NS passenger year 1933-35 confirmed.
Chocowinity - Zebulon construction: Wikipedia 'built 1910' contradicts a June 1908 N&S timetable through Greenville and Wilson to Raleigh.
Opening days 1881: 26 May vs 1 Jun (Elizabeth City), 13 Dec vs 6 Dec (Edenton) - NSHS vs carolana.
Colon - Cumnock: new 1914 line or the old Egypt Railroad grade.
Belhaven routing 1922-1932 (via Mackeys or via the Pinetown cutoff).
All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values except Ellerbe's 1923 headway and the 1946 Virginia Beach headway are estimates.
omitted: Durham Branch (Durham - Bonsal - Duncan, Durham & South Carolina leased 1920): no confirmed NS passenger year - report drawable NONE.
Cape Henry steam extension (Virginia Beach - Cape Henry, 1902-1904): no timetable or station list confirms passenger trains - NONE.
Munden ('Currituck') Branch, NS era: no NS-era passenger year found (the 1898 Guide anchor belongs to the NVB&S) - NONE.
Beckford Junction - Elizabeth City and Euclid - Kempsville - Providence Junction: no passenger evidence.
Norfolk Terminal Station approach (1912-1940): the report allows it only if traced separately; not traced (the N&W layer draws that track).

Predecessor companies' own eras (NVB&S, Chesapeake Transit, Suffolk & Carolina, Washington & Plymouth, Albemarle & Pantego, Raleigh & Cape Fear / Raleigh & Southport, Aberdeen & Asheboro, Durham & Charlotte, A&NC 1858-1904 and 1935-, Atlantic & East Carolina): separate companies needing their own research.

segments.note: Norfolk Southern main line (Norfolk Southern Railroad 1883, Norfolk and Southern Railroad 1891, Norfolk and Southern Railway 1906, Norfolk Southern Railroad 1910, Norfolk Southern Railway 1942 - receivership reorganizations of one operator). Norfolk - Edenton locals Nos. 5/6 and Norfolk - Raleigh Nos. 1/2 in Dec 1919 [Daily Advance 9 Dec 1919]; Pullman sleepers Raleigh - Norfolk from 5 Jun 1910; twice daily each way in 1914 and 1932, one round trip (Nos. 1/2) by 1942. NS trains used Norfolk Terminal Station until 15 May 1940, then a new Berkley station with a bus connection. The NC Utilities Commission granted discontinuance of Nos. 1/2 the week of 9 Jan 1948 and the last NS passenger trains ran 31 Jan 1948 (Wikipedia citing Cox). Freight continued (today Chesapeake & Albemarle) and is not drawn. Headway is an estimate from the twice-daily service (headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates, NOT sourced).
